Fleet Doctrine

Unlocks the Fleet Doctrine decision: learn how your crews fight. Plunder, raiding or slaving, or the doctrine of your own people: broadsides for Sartosa and Araby, Ramming Speed for the freebootaz, the Drowned Dead for the Vampire Coast, slave galleys for the Druchii.
Set Out

Unlocks the Set Out decision: put to sea for three to six months on a heading of your choice. Every sea has its own prizes, monsters, navies and wonders, and the sea's mood decides much of what you meet.
Set Out
Put to sea for a season of plunder. Choose a heading: your home waters or a neighbouring sea. Each sea of the world has its own prizes, monsters, navies and wonders.
You choose a heading and put to sea for three to six months.
You have not been at sea for the last five years
The [Root.GetSeaShips] are provisioned, the [Root.GetSeaCrew] sober enough to stand, and the tide turns at dawn. Your home waters are [Root.GetSeaHome]. Where away, Captain?
Set course for the Sea of Claws: Marienburg cogs, Norse longships, and ice.
Set course for the Great Western Ocean: Bretonnian coasts and the Mists of Albion.
Set course for the Tilean Sea: Sartosa, Tilean gold and the Pirate Coast.
Set course for the waters of Araby: spice dhows and the Sultan's war-galleys.
Set course for the Southern Sea: ivory, gems and long, dead calms.
Set course for the Lustrian seas: temple gold, sea serpents and the Vampire Coast.
Set course for the seas of Naggaroth: Black Arks, icebergs and slave markets.
Set course for the Inner Sea of Ulthuan: elven treasure and the Shifting Isles.
Set course for the Far Eastern seas: jade, junks and typhoons.
Set course for the Sea of Chaos: daemon ships and warp storms.
Set course for the Inner Ocean of the Under-Empire: warpstone and darkness.

A scrawny ship's cat has come aboard with the stores and made itself at home on the cable tier. The old hands swear a fed cat keeps [Root.GetSeaPower] in good temper. The boatswain swears it ate his supper.
Feed the beast. It is a good omen.
Over the side with it.

For three days a great white albatross has followed the ship, riding the wind off the stern. The [Root.GetSeaCrew] say it carries a drowned sailor's soul and must be left alone. Your best marksman says it would make a fine shot.
Let it fly.
Take the shot.
Before the tide turns, a holy one of your own people comes down the quay asking for passage: one who knows the ways of [Root.GetSeaPower]. Turning such a passenger away is thought very bad luck.
Welcome aboard.
There is no room.

The [Root.GetSeaCrew] have a petition: they want your ship renamed after your last great deed, so every port will know who comes. The oldest sailor aboard spits over the rail. Everyone knows a renamed ship is an unlucky ship.
Paint the new name on.
She keeps her old name.
On the last night ashore the [Root.GetSeaCrew] gather at the waterline and look at you. Something must go to [Root.GetSeaPower] before the voyage: gold, or blood.
Throw in a purse of gold.
Throw in a prisoner.
The sea gets nothing from me.

The [Root.GetSeaShips] limp back into harbour, barnacled and salt-white, low in the water with what is left of the plunder. In every tavern on the waterfront your [Root.GetSeaCrew] are already telling the tale, a little bigger each time.
Ashore at last.
A sail off [Root.GetSeaTheatre]! She is [Root.GetSeaPrize], wallowing low in the water and slow as a cow. Your [Root.GetSeaCrew] are already at the rail. [Root.GetSeaCry]
Board her!
Run up the colours and tell her to strike.
Take the crew for the pens.
The Code says she pays the toll and sails on.
She may get away.
The sky off [Root.GetSeaTheatre] goes the colour of a bruise. By noon the [Root.GetSeaShips] are climbing waves taller than their masts and the rigging screams in the wind.

This is no honest storm. The wind comes from every quarter at once, lightning walks on the water, and the old hands swear they hear laughter in the thunder. [Root.GetSeaPower] is angry with you, Captain, and the sea is [Root.GetSeaMood].
Lash the helm and ride it out.
Pray to [Root.GetSeaPower].
Run for the nearest shore. This voyage is over.
The voyage ends early: you sail for home.
The water off the bow boils and something comes up out of the deep: [Root.GetSeaMonster]. Its first pass takes the bowsprit. The [Root.GetSeaCrew] look at you.
Harpoons and boarding axes! We kill it!
Every sail aloft. Run!
Throw it a prisoner and sail on while it feeds.
Too long at sea, too little gold, and now the water casks taste of rot. You hear the [Root.GetSeaCrew] muttering below, and this morning someone nailed a black spot to your cabin door.
Hang the ringleaders from the yardarm.
Break open my own share and pay them.
I will fight the first mate for the ship, here and now.
Another captain crosses your bow off [Root.GetSeaTheatre], flying no flag you know, and runs out her guns to see what you will do.

A hulk comes out of the fog with weed on her hull and dead men in her rigging, and on her quarterdeck stands Luthor Harkon himself, the mad vampire admiral of the Vampire Coast, shouting orders to a crew that drowned centuries ago. He sees you, and grins with too many teeth.

A black ravenship slides out of the sun, and the sea-dragon cloak on her captain tells you who he is: Lokhir Fellheart, the Krakenlord, Druchii raider of a hundred coasts. He raises a gauntleted hand, half salute and half challenge.

Cold mist, and then a Druchii warship close enough to see her captain: Duriath Helbane, the Lord of Khand, who has bled Ulthuan's coasts for longer than your grandfather's grandfather lived. His corsairs are already at the rail.
A dragon-headed longship from Skeggi, the Norse town on the edge of Lustria, swings across your bow, and the jarl himself stands in her prow, axe on his shoulder, measuring you up.
Run out the guns!
Hail her and parley.
Give her a wide berth.
An old friend! Break out a bottle and trade the news.
A ship drifts across your course with torn sails and no one at the helm. Her decks are empty and her boats still lashed in place. Whatever happened to her crew, it happened quickly.
Board her and search the hold.
Burn her as an offering to [Root.GetSeaPower].
Leave her to the sea.
The hold is empty.
The lookout sights land where the charts show only sea: an island off [Root.GetSeaTheatre], green and empty, with a sheltered cove and fresh water. No one has a name for it.
Chart it. Someone will pay for this map.
Bury a chest of plunder here for leaner years.
Maroon the troublemakers here.
In a few years you may come back to dig it up.
Sails off the Wasteland coast: the Imperial Navy out of Dietershafen, great carracks with Sigmar's comet on their banners, and they are hunting pirates.
Longships out of Norsca, a whole raiding fleet of them, shields along their sides, and they have seen you.
A Bretonnian sea lord's galleons bear down from the coast of Lyonesse, pennants streaming, knights in full armour on their decks.
White hulls and swan-winged prows: a squadron of the Lothern Sea Guard, the finest sailors in the world, on patrol for raiders.
The black flags of Sartosa! A Pirate Prince's squadron, and they do not share their waters.
An Estalian treasure fleet's escorts, tall galleons with priests of Myrmidia at the prow, turn to bar your way.
The Sultan's war-galleys, banks of oars beating, close in under lateen sails. Araby does not love freebooters it cannot tax.
The fog thickens and the drowned fleet of the Vampire Coast comes out of it: rotting hulks crewed by the dead, cannons crusted with coral, the sea itself heaving them along.
Reed-hulled war canoes of the Lizardmen pour out of a river mouth, skinks shrieking at the paddles, a great Saurus in each prow.
Swift Amazon war canoes slip out of the mangroves, their warriors armed with strange old weapons that glow at the tips.
A Black Ark: a floating fortress of black towers and dungeons, bigger than a city, with a swarm of reaver ships around it like crows round a gibbet. The Druchii have smelled slaves.
A squadron of Cathayan war-junks, red sails ribbed like dragons' wings, and they carry cannon that fire black powder rockets.
Ships that are not ships: hulls of bone and burning sails, crewed by things that should not exist. The warp has spat out a daemon fleet.
Rat-ships of a rival clan come squealing out of a side-tunnel, warpfire throwers glowing green at their bows.
A squadron of pirate-hunters, paid by the merchant houses of a dozen ports, has found you at last.
Give battle!
Crowd on every sail and run.
Pay them off.
You may get away clean.
You put in at [Root.GetSeaPort] to take on water and unload what you can. The waterfront is noisy, crooked and very welcoming to anyone with gold to spend.
Sell the plunder.
A night to remember in the taverns.
Hire more hands.
Buy charts of the far coasts.

For days the wind has been at your back and the sea as smooth as glass. On the last night a great school of dolphins swims alongside, and the old hands say [Root.GetSeaPower] has taken a liking to you.

The sea, [Root.GetSeaMood], heaves itself up off the bow and something stands on the water: a servant of [Root.GetSeaPower], shaped of foam and green rage, whose voice is the grinding of the deep. It names a price for your ship.
Thanks be to [Root.GetSeaPower].
Pay the price.
I bow to no fish!
Karybdis, the great whirlpool of the Sea of Claws, opens off the starboard bow, and at its rim pack ice grinds like teeth. Sailors say the wreck at its heart is full of gold.
At midnight a ship crosses your bow, lit from within, her crew standing at their posts with the patience of the dead. A ghost ship of the Great Ocean, and her captain beckons you to follow.
Lights on the shore off the Pirate Coast, swinging like lanterns on a quay. Wreckers' lights, set to lure ships onto the rocks, and the wreckers will be rich.
The reefs off Araby sing at dusk. The sailors say a djinn is bound beneath them and grants a wish to any captain bold enough to sail the reef by night.
The wind dies. For weeks the Southern Sea lies flat as a mirror and the water casks run low. Far off, a smudge of smoke rises from an island no chart shows.

A song comes over the water off Lustria, sweet as honey. The crew drift towards the rail. You know the tales: the siren calls of the Vampire Coast, that drag ships onto the reefs where the drowned wait.
An iceberg looms out of a sorcerous mist off Naggaroth, and frozen in its heart, perfectly preserved, is a Druchii ravenship with her crew still at the oars.
The Shifting Isles: islands that move in the night, harbours that open and close like mouths, and somewhere among them, an elven treasure the Asur hid long ago.
A typhoon is coming out of the east, a wall of black cloud from sea to sky. Ahead of it, driven by the wind, a fleet of Cathayan junks runs for shelter, heavy with cargo.
A warp storm boils over the Sea of Chaos, and inside it the sea runs uphill. At its heart something glows: raw warpstone, falling like hail.
The cavern roof groans. Ahead, the Run narrows under a hanging mass of rock that sheds dust with every heartbeat, and beyond it lies a forgotten Dwarf vault.
Steer into it.
Give it a wide berth.
A fishing coast, lamps out, nets on the shingle, every soul asleep. Your [Root.GetSeaCrew] grin and slip the boats over the side.
Fill the pens.
Another night.
Years ago you buried a chest on a nameless island. Today you are back with a spade, a map, and a crew that wants to watch.
Dig!
Someone has already dug it up.
The map was wrong all along.

This commander takes longships far up the rivers, strikes and is gone before the levies gather.

The Freigattur needs captains who know their trade, the old Sea King tells you, leaning on the gunwale of a longship drawn up on the shingle. "Do you raid fast and run, do you hold the shield-wall, or do you take the ships up the rivers where no one expects us?"
Broadsides. Every gun at once.
Ramming Speed!
The drowned dead. They never tire and never break.
The slave galleys. Hunt them down and chain them to the oars.
Raid fast and run.
The shield-wall.
Up the rivers, where no one expects us.
Refit the Flagship

Unlocks the Refit the Flagship decision: lay down the next ship in the line without waiting for the shipwrights. A first hull for 100 gold, a proper flagship for 200 gold and three deeds at sea, and a great flagship for 400 gold and six deeds. Five years between refits.
Recruit Raiders

Unlocks the Recruit Raiders decision: muster a standing band of your own people at your capital for prestige and Infamy. Corsairs and Dreadspears for the Druchii, cutlasses and pistols for Sartosa, scimitars for Araby, boyz for the freebootaz, the drowned for the Vampire Coast. Half upkeep, kept in peace, and gone when you die.
Refit the Flagship
Empty the yards and lay down the next ship in the line: a first hull, then a proper flagship, then a great one that every port on the coast will know by her sails.
Raise a Dragon-ship
Fell the tallest pines of the fjord and raise a ship worthy of the saga: first a longship of your own, then a dragon-ship, then a great dragon whose head the skalds will sing of.
Recruit Raiders
Spread the word along the waterfront: there is plunder to be had under your flag. A band of [Root.GetSeaRaiders] will muster at your capital.
Five years have passed since the last refit
Has done at least three deeds at sea
Has done at least six deeds at sea
Has no raider band in the field already
Has not mustered raiders in the last five years
A raider band of your own people musters at your capital. It costs half upkeep, stays in peace and breaks up when you die.
Raiders Mustered
A band of raiders was mustered not long ago. The waterfront needs time to forget the last lot.

The sloop came round the headland at dawn, low in the water and running hard, and my [Root.GetSeaCrew] ran her down before the sun was a hand above the sea. Her captain went over the side rather than face me. She is fast, she is sound, and she is too good to sell. A captain should have a ship that is known: a [Root.GetSeaFlagship] to fly my colours from.

The shipwright found me in the tavern, or I found him: neither of us remembers. He has a hull on his slip, a fine one, built for a patron who drowned before he could pay. 'Fifty crowns,' he says, 'and she's yours. Forty if you stand me another.' He has been drinking since noon and he will not be sober until the hull is sold. A [Root.GetSeaFlagship] of my own...

The storm drove her onto the bar beneath my walls: a big ship, bigger than anything in my harbour, with her masts gone and her hold full of sand. No one came ashore from her. The fishermen say she is cursed. The fishermen say that about everything. With enough hands and enough rope she could float again, and she would make a [Root.GetSeaFlagship] fit to be feared.
The prize is mine.
Pay the man.
Pour him another. And another.
Raise her!
The drowned will raise her for me.
I have no use for a ship.

The shipwrights came up from the yards with their caps in their hands and their plans under their arms. My ship has carried me through enough, they say, and the timber is tired. For 200 gold they will lay down a proper flagship, a [Root.GetSeaFlagship] with the guns and the hold to match my name. The old girl can become her tender.

The master shipwright has dreamed of this ship for thirty years, and now he thinks he has found the captain to build her for. For 400 gold he will empty every yard on the coast and raise a great flagship, a [Root.GetSeaFlagship] so large that rivals will strike their colours at the sight of her topsails.
Lay her keel!
She serves as she is.

The hull goes down the slip to the cheers of the waterfront and settles in the harbour as if she had always been there. She is small as flagships go, but she is mine, and every [Root.GetSeaCrew] on the coast knows which [Root.GetSeaShip] flies my colours.
The yards were emptied for her and the forests stripped for her mast. Now the new [Root.GetSeaFlagship] rides at anchor below my walls, and the old ship looks like a jolly-boat beside her.

Half the coast came to see her launched. She took the water like a falling tower, the wave of her rocked every boat in the harbour, and when she came up she was the greatest [Root.GetSeaFlagship] on any sea that I know of. Let them come against her.
Run up my colours.

Word went along the waterfront: plunder under my flag, and no questions asked. By the end of the week the quays were full of them, the [Root.GetSeaRaiders] of every tavern from here to the headland. They will sail for me, and fight for me, as long as there is gold to share and I am alive to share it.
[Root.GetSeaCry]
The Fortress of Eternal Torture

The greatest of the Black Arks, a mountain of black rock that rivals the White Tower's own Tor Koruali. Its dungeons go down further than its towers go up, and the screaming never stops. Maranith, called Caledor's Bane, has commanded it for longer than most kingdoms have stood, and his black dragon Wrath roosts on its highest spire.
The Throne of Black Tides

A wide, squat citadel ringed with slave-galleys like a spider with its young. From its throne hall Lord Venil Chillblade sends orders to every fleetmaster of the Black Ark fleets, and every fleetmaster obeys, or is replaced.
The Citadel of Drowning Screams

Its lower halls lie below the waterline, and the tide is let into the cells twice a day. Lady Drane Brackblood keeps the rolls of the Black Ark fleets here, and the fleetmasters who forget what they owe her come to learn the tide-tables by heart.
The Palace of Oblivion

Lost at sea long ago and searched for ever since: a palace of black marble and silver chains that went into the mists off the Shifting Isles and never came out. Some say it drifts still, crewed by the dead. Some say it waits for a captain worthy of it.
The Temple of Spite

A black ark crowned with a temple to Khaine, whose altar has not been dry in four thousand years. It was Athil Khairn's once, until Duriath Helbane took it from him with a single cut, and the priests did not even pause in their chanting.
The Black Serenade
Wind moans through the hollow towers of this ark night and day, a dirge that carries for leagues across the water. Sailors who hear it at night pray to every god they know. It does not help.
The Tower of Blessed Dread

A tall, narrow ark, its battlements lined with the skulls of sea-monsters. Lokhir Fellheart, the Krakenlord, has sailed it for centuries, and his reavers swear there is no coast in the world it has not darkened.
The Spire of Cold Lament
An ark of pale grey stone that sweats rime even in the southern seas. Its slave pens are so cold that the captives' breath freezes on the bars. The Druchii who crew it never seem to notice.
The Talon of Agony
A hooked spur of rock, its towers bent like a claw closing on prey. The Talon was lost when its fleetmaster turned on the Witch King, and no one in Naggarond will say what became of either.
The Harrow of the Deep

A jagged ark whose underside is a forest of iron chains and hooks, dragged along the seabed to catch whatever lives there. It came back from its last voyage empty of crew, and was laid up in the Sea of Malice to wait for a captain with a stronger stomach.
The Tower of Midnight

Hardly an ark at all: a single dark tower on a raft of rock, a border fortress that drifted out to sea when the world broke. Small as it is, it is still a castle afloat, and there are kings who would give their crowns for one.
The Bastion of Whispered Knives
A small, crooked ark riddled with secret passages. Three of its fleetmasters have died in their beds. The fourth sleeps in a different room every night, and still he does not sleep well.
The Keep of the Weeping Chain
A squat keep whose anchor chain is hung with the bones of those who failed it. In a high wind the bones knock together, and the sound has given the keep its name.
The Eyrie of Black Gulls
A sea-stack of an ark, its cliffs white with the droppings of the black gulls that follow it in clouds, feasting on what the pens throw overboard.
The Tower of Salt and Bone
A forgotten ark, crusted with salt, its towers patched with the bones of whales. It lies at anchor in a dead lagoon of the Sea of Malice, waiting for the Witch King to remember it.
The Watch of the Hag Moon
A watchtower ark sworn of old to the convents of the Hag Sorceresses. It has no fleetmaster now, and the sorceresses who keep it are said to be choosing one.
Attain a Black Ark

Unlocks the Attain a Black Ark decision: petition the Witch King for one of the arks held in reserve at Naggarond. Sixteen Black Arks sail the world's seas, small, middle and great, and every one is unique. An ark gives prestige and retinue, sails against your enemies once in every war, and fills the pens in years of war. It passes only to a Corsair heir.
Seize a Black Ark
Unlocks the Seize a Black Ark decision: challenge another Druchii captain for their ark, by storm or by gold. Once every ten years.
Attain a Black Ark
Send gold, slaves and a carefully worded letter to Naggarond. The Witch King keeps a few arks at anchor in the Sea of Malice for captains who have earned them. Perhaps he will think you one.
The Witch King answers the petition. He may grant an ark from the reserve, or keep the gifts and tell you to wait.
Seize a Black Ark
An ark belongs to whoever can hold it. Challenge [Root.GetTitledFirstName] for theirs.
You challenge the captain for their ark: by storm or by bribing the crew. The winner keeps it.
An ark waits in the Witch King's reserve
Has not petitioned Naggarond in the last five years
Has not challenged for an ark in the last ten years
The gifts stay in Naggarond. You may petition again in five years.
The ark drifts back into the mist, and is lost to you.
The ark's host lands at the enemy port nearest their capital in one to two months, if the war still runs.
Petitioned Naggarond
This character has lately asked the Witch King for a Black Ark.
Challenged for an Ark
This character has lately challenged a captain for their Black Ark.
Took my Black Ark

The reply came on black vellum, sealed with the Witch King's own sign. Malekith has looked on my deeds and found them sufficient. One of the arks at anchor in the Sea of Malice is mine: its towers, its pens, its corsairs and its screaming. I am to bring it back to him full.

The reply came, eventually. The gifts were received, the slaves have been put to good use, and the Witch King thanks me for my loyalty. Of the ark there was not a word. In Naggarond, silence is an answer. I am not yet enough.
The ark is mine.
I will be patient. For now.

She came out of the mist at dawn: a Black Ark, a mountain of dark stone drifting with no banners and no lights. No reaver ships circle her. No slaves wail in her pens. Whoever commanded her is dead, or worse, and the ark is waiting for someone to claim her. My [Root.GetSeaCrew] are pale, but they are watching me.
Board her. She is mine now.
Leave the cursed thing to the sea.

The ark of [From.GetTitledName] lies at anchor, guarded by corsairs who have not been paid in a month. I can take her by storm, through the sea gate at night with my best blades, or I can let gold do the work and have the gates opened from within. Either way, by morning she will fly my banner, or I will be hanging from hers.
Storm the sea gate!
Gold opens any gate.
[From.GetTitledName] came for my ark in the night, and by dawn it was theirs. My captains, my pens, my towers, all of it. I have not forgotten. I will not forget.
[From.GetTitledName] came for my ark in the night and found it held against them. Their corpses decorate the sea gate now, the ones we found, at least. The ark is mine still.
Let them come again.

A herald of Naggarond came to my hall today, dressed in black and carrying a single iron key. The Witch King has need of another fleetmaster. One of the arks in the reserve is to sail under my command, and I am to remember, every day, whose gift it is.
Kneel and accept.
The Ark Awaits

My [Root.GetSeaCrew] are at the walls and the pens are empty: the ark is ready to sail. Word is that [ark_enemy.GetTitledName] has ports enough near their capital. Send the ark, and in a month or two its host will come ashore at their door.
Send the ark!
The ark stays at anchor.

The watchtowers saw it first: a mountain of black stone on the horizon, coming on against the wind. By noon its reaver ships were on the beaches, and by evening the host of [From.GetTitledName] had come ashore. The Druchii have come for slaves.
To arms!
